# QueryCard

> Collapsible query card containing a UForm, with fields in a responsive grid.

Fields are laid out in a responsive grid (one column, two from md, four from xl, adjustable with `ui.grid`). The generic `S` is the schema.

## Usage

### Title and icon

`title` is the title text and `icon` is the icon to the left of the title; pass an empty string to hide the icon.

<component-example name="query-card-title">



</component-example>

### Collapsing

Control the expanded state with `v-model:open`, expanded by default. `expand-icon` is the button icon shown when collapsed, and `collapse-icon` is the button icon shown when expanded.

<component-example name="query-card-collapse">



</component-example>

- When validation fails while collapsed, the card expands automatically to show the errors. In the example, collapse it first, then press "Submit" in the props bar to see it.
- Collapsed fields cannot be focused or used.

### Disabled

`disabled` disables the fields in the form (using the disabled state of `UForm`); `submit()` and `clear()` on the template ref and the `submit` and `clear` provided by `#actions` do nothing. Buttons in `#actions` are not disabled automatically, so pass `disabled` yourself.

<component-example name="query-card-disabled">



</component-example>

### Columns

Adjust the number of columns with `ui.grid`. When changing columns, write out every breakpoint: tailwind-merge only replaces classes of the same breakpoint, so with only `md:grid-cols-3`, the built-in `xl:grid-cols-4` still applies.

<component-example name="query-card-grid">



</component-example>

You can also remove the built-in breakpoints with the function form and set your own:

```vue
<ShuoQueryCard
  :state="query"
  :ui="{
    grid: (defaults) =>
      defaults.replace(/(md|xl):grid-cols-\d/g, '') + ' lg:grid-cols-3'
  }"
>
  ...
</ShuoQueryCard>
```

See [Query field columns](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/theme/component-defaults#query-field-columns) for site-wide columns.

### Long titles

By default the title neither wraps nor truncates; when `header-right` does not fit, the whole block moves to the next line, aligned right, without squeezing the title or the collapse button. The title bar of `ShuoListCard` follows the same rules. To let a long title wrap next to the icon, override the title bar with `ui` so it does not wrap (`bar: 'flex-nowrap'`) and allow the title to shrink (`title: 'min-w-0 shrink whitespace-normal'`):

<component-example name="query-card-long-title">



</component-example>

## Examples

### Validation and action buttons

Press Enter in a field to submit; `submit` fires only after validation passes, with the data in `event.data`. Put the bottom buttons in `#actions`. `clear` fires the `clear` event; the page resets the data and the component then clears the validation errors.

<component-example name="query-card-basic">



</component-example>

### Submitting from the title bar

Call `submit()` and `clear()` through the template ref, for example to put the search button in `#header-right`.

<component-example name="query-card-expose">



</component-example>

### With ListCard

After submitting the query, call `getPagination(1)` on [ShuoListCard](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/layout/list-card) to query from the first page; changing pages keeps the submitted query.

<component-example name="query-card-with-list">



</component-example>

## Props

<component-props name="ShuoQueryCard">



</component-props>

`v-model:open` (`boolean`, default `true`) controls the expanded state.

# Table

> Plain table built on UTable, with skeleton, empty data and height transition.

It has no card, title or pagination, so it can go straight into a modal or your own `UCard`. Non-wrapping headers, cell padding, empty and loading texts, the first-load skeleton, `interactionDisabled`, and the height and fade transitions are all shared with [ShuoListCard](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/layout/list-card). The generic `T` is the row type.

## Usage

### Loading and empty data

`loading` means a query is in progress. When re-querying with existing data, the data fades and switches with a height transition; without data, the query shows "Loading…". After the data is cleared, `empty` is shown, "No data" by default.

<component-example name="table-basic">



</component-example>

Keep the existing `data` while re-querying and update it after the query succeeds, so the data fades instead of being cleared.

### First-load skeleton

When the component is created while loading (`loading` is `true`) with no data, three skeleton rows are shown based on the number of columns; after the first query finishes, the skeleton is no longer shown. Press "Recreate" to recreate the table in the loading state.

<component-example name="table-skeleton">



</component-example>

The skeleton column count uses leaf columns and excludes columns hidden by `tableProps.state.columnVisibility`.

### Transition

When the row count or content height changes, the data area height changes smoothly over 0.2 seconds; when re-querying with existing data, the data fades to 0.5 opacity. With `transition` set to `false`, the height follows the content directly and the fade has no transition. Nothing is animated when the user prefers reduced motion.

<component-example name="table-transition">



</component-example>

### Selection

`selectable` adds a selection column at the front, and the selection is bound to an array of keys with `v-model:selected`. `row-key` sets the key: a field name (such as `row-key="id"`) or a function that builds the key from the row; the selection keeps the original type of the keys. Select all in the header only selects the selectable rows on the current page, and shows an indeterminate state when only some are selected. With `select-all` set to `false`, the header shows the `selection-header` text instead.

<component-example name="table-selection">



</component-example>

- Without `row-key`, the row index (`'0'`, `'1'`…) is the key. The first row is still `'0'` after changing pages and selects different data, so always set it with server-side pagination.
- Selected keys are kept when changing pages or re-querying, including those on other pages; set `v-model:selected` to `[]` to clear the selection.
- All checkboxes are disabled while loading (`loading`).
- `select-all` can be set site-wide with `components.table.selectAll` in [Component defaults](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/theme/component-defaults).

### Rows that cannot be selected

Rows for which `row-selectable` returns `false` cannot be selected and are skipped by select all. In this example the key combines the year and number (such as `115-1`), and closed rows cannot be selected.

<component-example name="table-selection-disabled">



</component-example>

## Examples

### Editable table

Put Shuo input components in cell slots, with a title and bottom buttons from `UCard`.

<component-example name="table-editable">



</component-example>

### Detail table in a modal

To limit the height and keep the header fixed, set `ui.root` and `sticky` through `tableProps`, so the table itself scrolls and the header stays in place. The table is recreated each time the modal opens and shows skeleton rows while loading.

<component-example name="table-modal">



</component-example>

### Disabling actions while loading

Cell slots get an extra `interactionDisabled`, `true` while loading, to disable buttons in the rows.

<component-example name="table-interaction">



</component-example>

### Custom loading and empty content

Replace the built-in texts with `#loading` and `#empty`. `#loading` only shows when there is no data and it is not the first-load skeleton.

<component-example name="table-empty-slot">



</component-example>

### Selection checkbox styles

`checkbox-props` sets the appearance of the select-all and row checkboxes, which share the same settings. The width and alignment of the selection column cells are set with a column whose `id` is `select` in `columns`; see [Selection column position and custom cells](#selection-column-position-and-custom-cells).

<component-example name="table-selection-style">



</component-example>

    </td>

      </code>

      </code>
    </td>

        md
      </code>
      
       when not set
    </td>

      </code>

      </code>

      Icon when checked; the Nuxt UI <code>
        check
      </code>
      
       icon when not set
    </td>
  </tr>

    <td>
      <code>
        indeterminateIcon
      </code>
    </td>

      <code>
        string
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Icon when partly selected; the Nuxt UI <code>
        minus
      </code>
      
       icon when not set
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

- The type is `TableCheckboxProps`, importable from `#shuo-ui/components/ShuoTable.vue`.
- The checked state, disabled state and accessible names are controlled by the table and cannot be set with `checkbox-props`; the `card` style of `variant` does not fit in a table and is not available either.
- For different styles on the select-all and row checkboxes, put your own `UCheckbox` in the `#select-header` or `#select-cell` slot.
- It can be set site-wide with `components.table.checkboxProps` in [Component defaults](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/theme/component-defaults) (no functions). A `checkbox-props` passed on the page replaces the site-wide value as a whole instead of merging it.

### Selection column position and custom cells

The selection column is placed at the front by default. To place it elsewhere, add a column with `id` set to `select` to `columns`; the selection column takes its position, and the column's settings apply to it. `th` and `td` in `meta.class` each replace the built-in `w-px` (fitting the checkbox width); with only `td` set, the header keeps `w-px`.

```ts
const columns: TableColumn<Row>[] = [
  { accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name' },

  // Selection column after the name
  { id: 'select', meta: { class: { td: 'bg-muted' } } },

  { accessorKey: 'amount', header: 'Amount' }
];
```

The `#select-header` and `#select-cell` slots replace the built-in select-all and row checkboxes, with the same props as `UTable`: for example `row.getIsSelected()` for the state, `row.toggleSelected()` to toggle it, and `row.getCanSelect()` to check whether the row can be selected.

## Props

<component-props name="ShuoTable">



</component-props>

`tableProps.paginationOptions.manualPagination` is always `true`, with pagination handled by the back end; column visibility comes from `tableProps.state.columnVisibility`, and `tableProps.columnVisibility` passed directly has no effect.

With `selectable` on, the selection is controlled by `v-model:selected`, and `rowSelection` and `onUpdate:rowSelection` in `tableProps` have no effect; without it you can still control selection through `tableProps` as with `UTable`. `row-key` is also used as the `getRowId` of `UTable` when selection is off.

"Loading…" and "No data" switch with the locale ("查詢中…" and "查無資料" in Traditional Chinese), and can be overridden globally with the `table.loading` and `table.empty` texts; see [Locales and messages](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/theme/messages). The accessible names of the select-all and row checkboxes ("Select all", "Select row") and the header text when select all is off (empty by default) come from `table.selectAll`, `table.selectRow` and `table.selectionHeader`. Set styles for headers, cells and so on with `tableProps.ui`, merged with the built-in styles.

<tbody>
  <tr>

# Shared props

> Props shared by the form input components, skeleton behavior and the empty-value contract.

## Playground

Use the selects above to switch size and state, and every component below changes together. The disabled, loading and skeleton states map to `disabled`, `loading` and `skeleton`; to make comparison easy, only one is on at a time. The four props are passed to each component at once with `v-bind`; in your own code, write them as ordinary props, for example `<ShuoInputText v-model="name" size="md" :loading="pending" />`.

<component-example name="common-playground">



</component-example>

## Shared props

The form input components (`ShuoInputText`, `ShuoInputNumber`, `ShuoSelectMenu`, `ShuoDatepicker`, `ShuoCheckbox`, `ShuoCheckboxGroup`, `ShuoRadioGroup`, `ShuoSwitch`, `ShuoTextarea`, `ShuoFile`, `ShuoMonths`, `ShuoPhone`) all support the props below, which are not repeated on each component page:

<field-group>
<field name="size" type="'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl'" default="lg">

Component size; components of the same size have the same height. When not passed, it falls back to the `size` of `UFormField`, then the site-wide setting, and finally `lg`. See [Size and UFormField](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/theme/component-defaults#size-and-uformfield).

</field>

<field name="disabled" type="boolean">

Disables the component. When not set, it follows the disabled state of `UForm`.

</field>

<field name="loading" type="boolean" default="false">

Shows a spinner and disables interaction.

</field>

<field name="skeleton" type="boolean" default="false">

Covers the component with a skeleton and pauses interaction while keeping the layout. The bound value is kept when switching back, and form validation is not affected.

</field>

<field name="id" type="string">

Input id; when not set, it follows `UFormField`. On `ShuoMonths` it points to the years input (the total months input in narrow containers), on `ShuoPhone` to the area code input; `ShuoFile` only follows `UFormField`.

</field>

<field name="name" type="string">

Field name; when not set, it follows `UFormField`.

</field>
</field-group>

Except for `ShuoDatepicker` (which uses `state` instead; see [Datepicker](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/date/datepicker)) and `ShuoFile`, components also support Nuxt UI's `color` (component color). Input-style components other than `ShuoDatepicker` and `ShuoFile` also support `highlight` (emphasized border); checkboxes and groups have no border and do not support `highlight`. The color and error border of `ShuoFile` follow `UFormField`.

### With UForm and UFormField

Wrap the component in `UFormField` with `name` matching the schema field. The component picks up the id, size, disabled and error state of `UFormField`, and triggers validation on input, blur and change:

```vue
<!-- Name -->
<UFormField label="Name" name="name" required>
  <ShuoInputText v-model="state.name" />
</UFormField>
```

None of the components below pass `size` or `disabled`: the size comes from `UFormField` and the disabled state from `UForm`. Press "Submit" first to see the error borders and messages of empty fields; fill everything in and submit again to see a notification with the submitted data.

<component-example name="common-form-field">



</component-example>

### Color and highlight

`color` changes the focus border and the selection color; `highlight` keeps the input border in that color without focus (not supported by checkboxes and groups). `ShuoDatepicker` has no `color`; it uses `state` for the validation result (`false` for error, `true` for success).

<component-example name="common-color">



</component-example>

## Built on Nuxt UI

Shuo components that wrap a Nuxt UI component inherit the props types of the underlying component, so Nuxt UI props that are not redeclared also get autocompletion and type checking. Event arguments are typed too. Slots are forwarded to the underlying component, and the same refs as the underlying component are exposed.

</table>

- Inherited props are only used for type inference; at runtime they are passed to the underlying component through `$attrs`.
- Props the component handles itself are not inherited and do not show up in autocompletion, such as `modelValue`. Input-style components (`ShuoInputText`, `ShuoInputNumber`, `ShuoTextarea`, `ShuoFile`) show their own loading icon, always using Nuxt UI's `appConfig.ui.icons.loading`, so `loadingIcon` is excluded as well and has no effect. `ShuoSelectMenu` lets `USelectMenu` show the loading icon, so `loadingIcon` works as usual.
- Events are forwarded to the underlying component through `$attrs` as usual, with types taken from the underlying component's emits; for example, the argument of `@blur` is a `FocusEvent`.
- Checkboxes, switches and groups support descriptions (`description`; for groups, the item's `description` field or the field set by `descriptionKey`): without a description the height matches an input of the same size; with one, the item grows and the description wraps, while its first line still lines up with fields without a description. The label stays on one line and is truncated with a tooltip showing the full text.
- Checkboxes and groups do not support Nuxt UI's `variant` (card, table), `indicator` or `highlight`: the border and padding of card and table make options taller; `indicator` moves the checkbox, while the loading spinner stays where the left checkbox is; `highlight` only changes the border color of card and table. Passing them is a type error and they are not applied at runtime.

### Slots

Input-style components can use `#leading` and `#trailing` to put icons or buttons before and after the input; `ShuoSelectMenu` can use every slot of `USelectMenu`. Checkboxes and groups have their own `#append` and `#item-append` for content next to the option label.

<component-example name="common-slots">



</component-example>

- The `#trailing` of `ShuoInputNumber` sits next to the unit and the loading icon without replacing them.
- See the component pages for the slot props, for example [Item append content](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/choice/radio-group#item-append-content).

### Exposed refs

After getting the component with a template ref, use the refs in the table to work with the underlying native elements, for example to focus, select all or open the menu.

<component-example name="common-expose">



</component-example>

## Skeleton

The skeleton keeps the layout space of the original control, following `size`, width, textarea rows and the option group layout, with no fixed height of its own. While it is on, the component cannot be clicked or used with the keyboard, and tooltips and open menus close.

A common use is an edit page loading data from the back end, with one loading state controlling the skeleton of every field. Press "Reload data" to try it: the layout stays the same during the skeleton, and the data fills in when it arrives.

<component-example name="common-skeleton">



</component-example>

Compared with `loading`: `loading` keeps the current value and shows a spinner inside the field, suited to a field doing its own work (such as fetching select options); `skeleton` covers the whole field, suited to when the page data has not arrived yet and the current value means nothing.

## Locales

Component texts (placeholders, accessible names, validation messages, date picker texts and so on) follow the Nuxt UI locale (`<UApp :locale>`), with Traditional Chinese and English built in; components already on screen update immediately when it changes. The default texts mentioned on these pages are the English ones. Text props passed explicitly (such as `title` or `placeholder`) are not affected by the locale. See [Locales and messages](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/theme/messages) for setup and overrides.

"Component language" in the palette menu at the top right of the docs site switches the language of the component examples on the page; by default it follows the docs language.

## Empty values

When the parent binds `null` / `undefined`, the components below write back the agreed empty value; unexpected values such as wrong types are also cleared to the agreed empty value. This applies both on mount and when the parent fills values in later. When clearing an unexpected value, `ShuoInputText`, `ShuoTextarea`, `ShuoInputNumber`, `ShuoRadioGroup`, `ShuoPhone` and `ShuoDatepicker` log a `console.warn` (`[ShuoComponentName] … cleared`); `ShuoSelectMenu` and `ShuoMonths` only clear, without a warning.

Press "Apply null from the back end" to simulate the back end returning `null` for every field: the bound values below change to each component's agreed empty value. `ShuoCheckboxGroup` does not write back and stays `null`.

<component-example name="common-empty-value">



</component-example>

These components do not write back the parent's value:

- `ShuoCheckboxGroup`: `null` or a non-array value shows everything unchecked; checking an option writes back the full array. Clearing gives `[]`.
- `ShuoCheckbox`: shows unchecked when the bound value is not `trueValue`.
- `ShuoFile`: `null` after clearing.


# File

> Single file selection and existing attachment download; selecting a file does not upload it.

`v-model: File | null`, required; selecting a file does not upload it.

## Usage

### Selecting a file

Binds the original `File`; `null` after clearing. Click the field, or focus it and press Enter or Space, to open the file dialog. `accept` only filters the file dialog and does not block other types; validate type limits with form rules.

<component-example name="file-basic">



</component-example>

### Existing attachments

Without a local `File`, `file-name` is shown. Pressing download fetches the contents of `file-url` as a Blob; cross-origin URLs must allow CORS, and a failed download shows a toast (requires `UApp`). When the file name is truncated, hovering or keyboard focus shows the full name, or a long press on touch devices (see [Tooltip](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/helper/tooltip#touch-long-press)); a long press does not open the file dialog.

<component-example name="file-existing">



</component-example>

### Button icons

`select-icon` is the select button shown when there is no file, `clear-icon` is the clear button, and `download-icon` is the download button shown when there is a file. The clear button only shows with a local `File` and when not disabled.

<component-example name="file-icons">



</component-example>

### Variants

Uses the `variant` and `icon` of `UInput`. `ShuoFile` has no `color` or `highlight`; the color and error border follow `UFormField`.

<component-example name="file-variant">



</component-example>

### Size and states

When disabled, the clear button is hidden but an existing attachment can still be downloaded; while loading, a spinner replaces the trailing buttons and nothing can be used. See [Shared props](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/overview/common) for the behavior shared by all states.

<component-example name="file-states">



</component-example>

## Examples

### With form validation

Check required, type and size with Valibot's `v.file`, `v.mimeType` and `v.maxSize`; `accept` only affects the file dialog, and the schema is the real limit.

<component-example name="file-validation">



</component-example>

### Uploading after selection

Selecting a file does not upload it; the page decides when to send the `File` in `v-model`. In the example, pressing "Upload" disables the field with `loading`, then clears `v-model` when done and shows the file as an existing attachment with `file-name` and `file-url`.

<component-example name="file-upload">



</component-example>

### Accessing the native input

Get the native input that shows the file name through `inputRef` on the template ref.

<component-example name="file-expose">



</component-example>

## Props

<component-props name="ShuoFile">



</component-props>

See [Shared props](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/overview/common#shared-props) for the behavior of `size`, `disabled`, `loading` and `skeleton`. The trailing area is always the clear and download buttons, so `trailing` and `trailingIcon` are not available; the id and error appearance come from `UFormField`.

# Phone

> Landline number with separate inputs for the area code and the number.

`v-model: string` (the full number), plus `v-model:area-code` and `v-model:number`; see [v-model](#v-model) below.

## Usage

### Binding

The three bindings update together; the full number is the area code plus the number, with no separator. Press "Read bound values" to show the current three values in a notification.

<component-example name="phone-basic">



</component-example>

- All three keep strings and leading `0`s; for example, area code `02` and number `00123456` give the full number `0200123456`.
- When the user types or pastes, only half-width digits are kept; values filled in by the parent are shown as is, and are only filtered after the user edits that input.
- When the area code or number has the wrong type, only that input is cleared and the full number is joined again; when the full number has the wrong type, both inputs are cleared.

### Filling in only the full number

When only the full number is filled in, it is split by a known area code that matches its prefix; without a usable area code, the whole number goes into the number input and the area code is cleared, with no guessing by length. To split it into both inputs, also bind `v-model:area-code` with a known area code. Switch `area-code` to compare the two results:

<component-example name="phone-split">



</component-example>

### Variants

Uses the `color` and `highlight` of `UInput`, applied to both the area code and number inputs.

<component-example name="phone-color">



</component-example>

### Size and states

While loading, a spinner shows at the far right of the number input and both inputs are disabled. See [Shared props](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/overview/common) for the behavior shared by all states.

<component-example name="phone-states">



</component-example>

## Examples

### With form validation

The component has no built-in rules for phone number length or valid area codes; define them in the form schema. The example checks required with `requiredText`, then the format of the full number with `v.regex`.

<component-example name="phone-validation">



</component-example>

### Storing area code and number separately

When the back end stores two fields, bind only `v-model:area-code` and `v-model:number`. Press "Load data" to simulate fetching from the back end, with `loading` disabling input meanwhile.

<component-example name="phone-parts">



</component-example>

## v-model

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      v-model
    </th>

      Type
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Description
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

# InputNumber

> Number input that shows thousands separators on blur, with decimal places and units.

`v-model: number | null`.

## Usage

### Decimal places and thousands separators

`decimal` defaults to `false`, allowing only integers; a positive integer sets the number of decimal places, and `true` allows any number. `thousand-separator` defaults to `true`, showing thousands separators on blur; pass `false` for numbers such as years or codes that should not have them.

<component-example name="input-number-decimal">



</component-example>

- While typing, the sign, decimal point and trailing zeros are kept; incomplete input (such as just `-`) binds `null`. On blur, the value is rounded and padded according to `decimal`, and thousands separators are shown.
- Non-numeric characters and decimals beyond the set places cannot be typed, and pasted text is reverted too. When `decimal` is `false` or `0`, the decimal point cannot be typed.
- On focus, the text switches to the editable form without separators. `inputmode` is `numeric` when `decimal` is `false` or `0`, and `decimal` otherwise, so phones show the matching number keyboard.

<tip>

The component has no `min` or `max`. It is a text input underneath, so the native `min`, `max` and `step` have no effect. Use [validation rules](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/form/validation) for ranges; see [With form validation](#with-form-validation) below.

</tip>

### Unit

When `unit` is `true`, "NTD" is shown ("元" in Traditional Chinese, switching with the locale). The text can be changed in [Locales and messages](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/theme/messages#overridable-items); passing a string shows that text. Units vary in length, so the right padding follows the unit's actual width and the number never overlaps the unit.

<component-example name="input-number-unit">



</component-example>

`unit` and `thousand-separator` can also have site-wide defaults; see [Configurable props](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/theme/component-defaults#configurable-props). The site-wide `unit` only accepts `true` / `false`.

### Variants

Uses the `variant`, `color` and `highlight` of `UInput`.

<component-example name="input-number-variant">



</component-example>

### Icon

Uses the `icon` of `UInput`, shown on the left alongside the unit.

<component-example name="input-number-icon">



</component-example>

### Size and states

While loading, the spinner sits to the right of the unit and the number and unit move left to make room. See [Shared props](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/overview/common) for the behavior shared by all states.

<component-example name="input-number-states">



</component-example>

## Examples

### With form validation

Use `requiredNumber` for required fields and add ranges with `v.minValue` and `v.maxValue`; use `optionalNonNegativeNumber` for optional non-negative numbers. What gets validated and submitted is a number, without separators.

<component-example name="input-number-validation">



</component-example>

### Centered numbers

`ui.base` has a built-in `text-right`; pass `text-center` to center the number, which suits short fields inside a sentence. With a unit or while loading, the right padding follows the trailing content's actual width, so the number never overlaps the unit.

<component-example name="input-number-center">



</component-example>

### Clear button

Put a clear button in `#trailing`. `#trailing` sits next to the unit and the loading icon without replacing them; see [Slots](#slots) below.

<component-example name="input-number-clearable">



</component-example>

### Accessing the native input

Get the native input through `inputRef` on the template ref.

<component-example name="input-number-expose">



</component-example>

<component-props name="ShuoInputNumber">



</component-props>

See [Shared props](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/overview/common#shared-props) for the behavior of `size`, `disabled`, `loading`, `skeleton`, `id` and `name`.

When centered, the number is centered in the space left after the unit and never overlaps it.

# InputText

> Single-line text input that can mask all or the last few characters.

`v-model: string`.

## Usage

### Mask

When `mask` is `true`, everything is masked; a positive integer masks that many trailing characters. The eye button on the right toggles between plain text and masked, and `hide-mask-toggle` hides that button. `v-model` always keeps the original text.

<component-example name="input-text-mask">



</component-example>

- `12345678` with `:mask="4"` shows `1234••••`; with fewer than four characters, everything is masked. `false`, `0`, negative numbers and non-finite numbers disable masking, and decimals are rounded down.
- Copying and cutting are blocked while masked; after revealing the text, copying works normally.
- Changing `mask` or `hideMaskToggle` dynamically resets to the masked state.
- When the text alignment is changed with `ui.base`, the partial mask overlay follows the alignment.

### Toggle icons

`reveal-icon` is shown while masked (press it to reveal the text), and `conceal-icon` is shown while the text is revealed (press it to mask again).

<component-example name="input-text-mask-icons">



</component-example>

### Variants

Uses the `variant`, `color` and `highlight` of `UInput`.

<component-example name="input-text-variant">



</component-example>

### Icon

Uses the `icon` of `UInput`; when `trailing` is `true`, the icon goes on the right.

<component-example name="input-text-icon">



</component-example>

### Size and states

When disabled, the text can still be revealed; during the skeleton it cannot be used. See [Shared props](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/overview/common) for the behavior shared by all states.

<component-example name="input-text-states">



</component-example>

## Examples

### With form validation

Use `requiredText` for required fields and check the format separately with `v.regex`. Masking only affects the display; the original text is what gets validated and submitted.

<component-example name="input-text-validation">



</component-example>

### Leading icon with mask

`#leading` goes on the left while the eye button stays on the right, so both can be used together.

<component-example name="input-text-leading-mask">



</component-example>

### Clear button

Put a clear button in `#trailing`. When masked or loading, the trailing position shows the eye button or the loading icon first; see [Slots](#slots) below.

<component-example name="input-text-clearable">



</component-example>

### Accessing the native input

Get the native input through `inputRef` on the template ref.

<component-example name="input-text-expose">



</component-example>

## Props

<component-props name="ShuoInputText">



</component-props>

See [Shared props](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/overview/common#shared-props) for the behavior of `size`, `disabled`, `loading`, `skeleton`, `id` and `name`. `type` is decided by `mask` and cannot be passed.

# Textarea

> Multi-line text input that keeps line breaks and can resize automatically.

`v-model: string`, keeping line breaks.

## Usage

### Rows and auto height

`rows` is the base number of rows (Nuxt UI defaults to `3`). When `autoresize` is `true`, the height grows with the content, from at least `rows` rows up to `maxrows` rows, after which a scrollbar appears; `maxrows` of `0` means no limit.

<component-example name="textarea-autoresize">



</component-example>

- Without `autoresize`, the height can be dragged up and down, but not below a single-line input of the same size; with it, dragging is disabled.
- `autoresize`, `rows`, `maxrows` and `fixed` can have site-wide defaults; see [Configurable props](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/theme/component-defaults#configurable-props).

### Variants

Uses the `variant`, `color` and `highlight` of `UTextarea`.

<component-example name="textarea-variant">



</component-example>

### Icon

Uses the `icon` of `UTextarea`; when `trailing` is `true`, the icon goes on the right.

<component-example name="textarea-icon">



</component-example>

### Size and states

While loading, a spinner shows in the top right corner, in the same place as Nuxt UI's trailing icon, without replacing the left `icon` or shifting where the text starts. The skeleton keeps the height of `rows`. See [Shared props](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/overview/common) for the behavior shared by all states.

<component-example name="textarea-states">



</component-example>

## Examples

### With form validation

Use `requiredText` for required fields, which also rejects whitespace only; check a minimum length separately with `v.minLength`.

<component-example name="textarea-validation">



</component-example>

### Character limit and counter

`maxlength` is the native character limit; once reached, nothing more can be typed. Show the current count with the `hint` of `UFormField`.

<component-example name="textarea-maxlength">



</component-example>

### Submitting with a shortcut

Events are forwarded to the native textarea, so keyboard modifiers work directly. In this example, Ctrl+Enter (⌘+Enter on macOS) posts the comment, while Enter alone still adds a line break.

<component-example name="textarea-shortcut">



</component-example>

### Accessing the native textarea

Get the native textarea through `textareaRef` on the template ref; `autoResize()` recalculates the auto height from the content. See [Expose](#expose) below.

<component-example name="textarea-expose">



</component-example>

</component-props>

See [Shared props](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/overview/common#shared-props) for the behavior of `size`, `disabled`, `loading`, `skeleton`, `id` and `name`.

# Auto-imports and types

> Auto-imported components and utilities, type aliases, and notes on using them with Nuxt UI.

      <code>
        formatDateDisplay
      </code>
      
      , <code>
        parseDateValue
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      ROC year display and date parsing; see <a href="https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/utils/format/date">
        Date
      </a>
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        formatNumberDisplay
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Thousands separators and decimal places; see <a href="https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/utils/format/number">
        Number
      </a>
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        splitPhone
      </code>
      
      , <code>
        joinPhone
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Splitting and joining area codes; see <a href="https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/utils/field/phone">
        Phone
      </a>
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        splitMonths
      </code>
      
      , <code>
        combineMonths
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Converting between total months and years/months; see <a href="https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/utils/field/months">
        Months
      </a>
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        resolveShuoDefault
      </code>
      
      , <code>
        getShuoComponentDefaults
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Effective values and raw settings of the component defaults; see <a href="https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/utils/settings/component-defaults">
        Component defaults
      </a>
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

Utilities and composables used inside the components are not auto-imported and are not part of the public API; they may change between versions.

## Types

Types can be imported from the `#shuo-ui` alias:

```ts
import type { DatepickerValue } from '#shuo-ui/components/ShuoDatepicker.vue';
import type { PageRequest } from '#shuo-ui/types/pagination';
import type { ShuoComponentDefaults } from '#shuo-ui/types/component-defaults';
```

Component props types can also be imported from `#shuo-ui/types/components` (such as `InputTextProps` and `SelectMenuProps`); importing them from the `.vue` files still works.

## Notes on using Nuxt UI

- Your project CSS must include `@import '@shuo/ui/css';` (after `@import 'tailwindcss'`). Otherwise Tailwind does not scan the classes inside the component library and some styles are missing.
- Wrap form fields in `UFormField` with a `name`. The component then picks up the id, name, size, disabled and error state of `UFormField`, and triggers validation on input, blur and change. See [Size and UFormField](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/theme/component-defaults#size-and-uformfield) for the size precedence.
- Icons use Iconify (`i-lucide-*`). Icons used by the component library, and icons set in `shuoUi.components`, are added to the `@nuxt/icon` client bundle by the module automatically. Other icons passed as props in your pages must be added to `icon.clientBundle.icons` yourself, or keep the runtime icon API. If your project disables the runtime icon API (`icon.provider: 'none'`), install `@iconify-json/lucide` so the icons can be bundled at build time.


# Validation

> Validate forms with UForm, UFormField and Valibot, using the built-in shared rules.

We recommend `UForm + UFormField` for forms and Valibot for validation schemas. The `name` of `UFormField` must match the field name in the schema and state; `required` only shows the required asterisk, and the schema decides whether a field is actually required.

## Shared rules

The rules are auto-imported by the module. Each form composes its own schema, and business rules stay out of the input components. See [Validation](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/utils/form/validation) under Utilities for the parameters and behavior of each rule:

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      Rule
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Fields
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        requiredText('Field name')
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Text, string values of select menus and radio groups, date strings, multi-line text
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        requiredNumber('Field name')
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Numbers
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        requiredArray('Field name', itemSchema)
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Checkbox groups, multiple select menus
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        optionalEmail('Field name')
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Optional email
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        optionalNonNegativeNumber('Field name')
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Optional non-negative numbers such as amounts, terms, scores and rates
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

The default error message is "field name + description", where the field name is the label on screen, for example "Name is required". Messages can be overridden with the module option `shuoUi.messages.validation`; see [Locales and messages](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/theme/messages).

```ts
import * as v from 'valibot';

const schema = v.object({
  name: requiredText('Name'),
  amount: requiredNumber('Amount'),
  email: v.pipe(requiredText('Email'), v.email('Email is invalid')),
  backupEmail: optionalEmail('Backup email'),
  approvedAmount: optionalNonNegativeNumber('Approved amount')
});
```

Add reusable format, length or range rules to the shared file; cross-field rules specific to one page stay in that form. Compose them with Valibot `pipe` instead of building a separate validation config language.

File fields (`ShuoFile`) bind `File | null`. Combine Valibot's `v.file`, `v.mimeType` and `v.maxSize` for required, type and size checks; see [With form validation](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/phone-file/file#with-form-validation) on the File page.

<note>

Dates and options are currently only checked for being required. Add rules for date formats, whether an option is still valid, cross-field conditions, numeric ranges and so on as needed, for example `v.pipe(v.number(), v.minValue(1), v.maxValue(100))`.

</note>

## Empty values and types

Components write `null` / `undefined` bound by the parent back as the agreed empty value (`''` for text, `null` for numbers, `[]` for date ranges and so on; see [Empty values](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/overview/common#empty-values)). Unexpected values are cleared, and most components also log a `console.warn` (`ShuoSelectMenu` and `ShuoMonths` only clear without warning; see the same section). An unselected radio group is `''`, so options should not use an empty string as their value.

The input types of the shared schemas accept `null` / `undefined` while editing, and the output after validation narrows to `string`, `number` or an array of the item type, so you do not need to change the components' empty-value contract.

## Display and interaction

- We recommend the built-in theme (`theme: true`) for error messages: a floating style inset in the field's bottom border that does not add to the field height. Keep enough spacing between fields, and avoid clipping overflowing content in the containers.
- `UForm` only fires `@submit` after validation passes; read the validated data from `event.data`. When validation fails, `@error` fires.
- Use the default validation timing on input, blur and change. When resetting, besides clearing the state, call the form's `clear()` to clear the errors.


# Installation

> Install and enable Shuo UI in a Nuxt project.

## Requirements

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      Package
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Version
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      Nuxt
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        ^4.6.2
      </code>
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        @nuxt/ui
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        ^4.12.0
      </code>
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

Runtime dependencies such as `date-fns`, `valibot` and `@vuepic/vue-datepicker` are installed along with the package.

## Steps

<steps level="3">

### Install the package

Pin a version with a tag, and change it to the new tag when upgrading. See [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/k90325248/shuo-ui/releases) for the changes in each version; every component page also ends with that component's changelog.

<code-group>

```bash [pnpm]
pnpm add github:k90325248/shuo-ui#v1.2.0
```

```bash [npm]
npm install github:k90325248/shuo-ui#v1.2.0
```

```bash [yarn]
yarn add github:k90325248/shuo-ui#v1.2.0
```

</code-group>

<tip>

We recommend also installing the lucide icon set (`pnpm add @iconify-json/lucide`): the built-in component icons (calendar, eye, download and so on) are then bundled into your site instead of being loaded from the network at runtime. Without it the components still work, and `@nuxt/icon` loads the icons at runtime.

</tip>

### Enable the module

`@nuxt/ui` must also be installed and listed in `modules`.

```ts [nuxt.config.ts]
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['@nuxt/ui', '@shuo/ui']
});
```

### Load the styles

Import Tailwind, Nuxt UI and the component library's source scan in your CSS.

```css [app/assets/css/main.css]
@import 'tailwindcss';
@import '@nuxt/ui';
@import '@shuo/ui/css';
```

Then register this file with `css` in `nuxt.config.ts`:

```ts [nuxt.config.ts]
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['@nuxt/ui', '@shuo/ui'],
  css: ['~/assets/css/main.css']
});
```

<warning>

The last line, `@import '@shuo/ui/css'`, makes Tailwind scan the classes used inside the component library (Tailwind does not scan `node_modules` by default). Without it, some styles (such as the loading icon size and layout) do not apply.

</warning>
</steps>

## Writing validation rules with Valibot

If your own code uses `import * as v from 'valibot'` to write schemas, install `valibot` in your project as well. pnpm does not let a project import a package's dependencies directly.

```bash
pnpm add valibot
```

## Locale

Component texts are in Traditional Chinese by default and follow the Nuxt UI locale (`<UApp :locale>`), with English built in. For an English-only project, set `shuoUi: { locale: 'en' }` in `nuxt.config.ts`; see [Locales and messages](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/theme/messages) for other options.

## Versions and upgrades

Versions are released as git tags (`vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`). When upgrading, update the tag in the install command and test your app.


# Introduction

> What Shuo UI is and where it fits.

Shuo UI is a set of form components built on [Nuxt UI](https://ui.nuxt.com) and shipped as a Nuxt module. It lets several projects share the same form components and behavior without giving up anything Nuxt UI already offers.

## Example

Below is a live `ShuoInputText`: type some text and the last 4 characters are masked. Click the eye button to toggle them.

<code-preview>
<shuo-input-text :mask="4" className="max-w-80" placeholder="Enter your ID number">



</shuo-input-text>

<template v-slot:code="">

```vue
<ShuoInputText v-model="value" :mask="4" placeholder="Enter your ID number" />
```

</template>
</code-preview>

## Features

- Traditional Chinese by default with English built in, following the Nuxt UI locale. Texts can be overridden per locale; see [Locales and messages](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/theme/messages)
- Styles use Nuxt UI semantic colors and CSS variables, so colors and themes come from your project
- Consistent size, disabled, loading (`loading`) and skeleton (`skeleton`) behavior
- Nuxt UI props, slots and refs that are not redeclared can be used directly, with full type inference
- Components and common [utilities](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/utils/form/validation) (validation rules, date and number display and more) are auto-imported


# Quick start

> Build your first form with UForm and Valibot, and meet every component.

## Your first form

Components start with `Shuo` and need no import. Use them with Nuxt UI's `UForm` and Valibot validation:

```vue
<template>
  <UForm :schema="schema" :state="state" @submit="onSubmit">
    <!-- Name -->
    <UFormField label="Name" name="name">
      <ShuoInputText v-model="state.name" />
    </UFormField>

    <!-- Amount -->
    <UFormField label="Amount" name="amount">
      <ShuoInputNumber v-model="state.amount" unit />
    </UFormField>

    <!-- Application date -->
    <UFormField label="Application date" name="date">
      <ShuoDatepicker v-model="state.date" clearable />
    </UFormField>

    <UButton type="submit" label="Submit" />
  </UForm>
</template>

<script setup lang="ts">
import * as v from 'valibot';

// requiredText and requiredNumber are auto-imported by the module
const schema = v.object({
  name: requiredText('Name'),
  amount: requiredNumber('Amount'),
  date: requiredText('Application date')
});

const state = reactive({
  name: '',
  amount: null as number | null,
  date: ''
});

const onSubmit = (event: { data: v.InferOutput<typeof schema> }) => {
  console.log(event.data);
};
</script>
```

<tip>

The `name` of `UFormField` must match the field name in the schema and state; the component then picks up the field's id, size, disabled and error state. See [Validation](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/form/validation) for the rules.

</tip>

# Component defaults

> Set size, display format, icons and other props site-wide with shuoUi.components.

Use `components` to set site-wide defaults per component, for example showing "value_label" in every select menu, or 20 rows per page in every list. The order of precedence is always:

```text
Prop passed explicitly on the component  >  Site-wide default (components.<component>)  >  Built-in default
```

`size` has one more layer, `UFormField`; see [Size and UFormField](#size-and-uformfield).

```ts [nuxt.config.ts]
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['@nuxt/ui', '@shuo/ui'],
  shuoUi: {
    components: {
      // selectMenu: select menu
      selectMenu: {
        format: '{value}_{label}',
        size: 'md',
        emptyValue: null,
        labelKey: 'Name',
        valueKey: 'Code'
      },

      // checkboxGroup: checkbox group
      checkboxGroup: {
        labelKey: 'Name',
        valueKey: 'Code'
      },

      // radioGroup: radio group
      radioGroup: {
        orientation: 'horizontal',
        breakpoint: 'lg',
        labelKey: 'Name',
        valueKey: 'Code'
      },

      // checkbox: checkbox
      checkbox: {
        trueValue: 'Y',
        falseValue: 'N'
      },

      // datepicker: date picker
      datepicker: {
        clearable: true,
        separator: '-'
      },

      // inputNumber: number input
      inputNumber: {
        unit: true, // The unit text comes from messages.inputNumber.unit
        thousandSeparator: true
      },

      // queryCard: query card
      queryCard: {
        ui: {
          // Query field columns: xl must be written explicitly
          // to override the built-in xl:grid-cols-4 (see below)
          grid: 'sm:grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-3 xl:grid-cols-3 2xl:grid-cols-4'
        }
      },

      // listCard: list card
      listCard: {
        pageSize: 20,
        ui: {
          title: 'text-lg' // Title bar ui parts are the same as queryCard
        }
      }
    }
  }
});
```

## Configurable props

The component key is the component name without `Shuo`, in camelCase, the same as in `messages`. It **does not change with prefix** (with `prefix: 'My'` you still write `components.selectMenu`).

Only the props in the table below can be set site-wide. State props such as `disabled`, `loading` and `skeleton`, and props tied to a single field (`id`, `name`, `items`, `mask`, `decimal`, `multiple` and so on) cannot.

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      Key
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Configurable props (built-in default)
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        inputText
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        size
      </code>
      
       (<code>
        lg
      </code>
      
      ), <code>
        hideMaskToggle
      </code>
      
       (<code>
        false
      </code>
      
      ), <code>
        revealIcon
      </code>
      
       (<code>
        i-lucide-eye
      </code>
      
      ), <code>
        concealIcon
      </code>
      
       (<code>
        i-lucide-eye-off
      </code>
      
      )
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>

Components or props outside this list cause a type error in `nuxt.config.ts`. Values that skip type checking (such as environment variables) are ignored at runtime with a console warning.

## Rules

- **"Passed explicitly" means the prop is written, whatever its value**: `<ShuoDatepicker :clearable="false" />`, `<ShuoSelectMenu :empty-value="null" />` and `format=""` all count as explicit and are not replaced by the site-wide value. `v-bind="{ clearable: undefined }"` counts as not written and uses the site-wide value.
- **ui is merged per slot**: with a site-wide `radioGroup.ui.fieldset` and a page passing `:ui="{ item: '...' }"`, both apply. If the page also passes `fieldset`, the page value replaces the site-wide one (classes are not concatenated). The result is then merged with the component's built-in styles using tailwind-merge, as in [Per-component `ui` prop](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/theme/theming#per-component-ui-prop). The title bar parts of `queryCard.ui` and `listCard.ui` (`bar`, `icon`, `title`, `headerRight`) share the same built-in styles; to make both cards' titles match, set the same values on both.
- **Other values are replaced as a whole**: arrays (such as `yearRange`) are not concatenated with the built-in value.
- `inputNumber.unit` site-wide only decides whether a unit is shown by default and only accepts `true` / `false`; the unit text comes from `messages.inputNumber.unit`. A single field can still pass `unit="pcs"` or `:unit="false"`.
- After setting `labelKey` / `valueKey` site-wide to `{ Code, Name }`, if a page's items are still `{ label, value }`, pass `label-key="label" value-key="value"` on that component. Radio and checkbox groups still bind string values, so convert numeric codes from the back end to strings first. In development mode, when items are missing a field, the console warning says whether the field name was passed explicitly or came from the site-wide setting (for example `(source: valueKey from the site-wide setting components.selectMenu.valueKey)`).

<warning>

The settings reach the browser through `runtimeConfig.public`, so they must be JSON-serializable: **no functions** (for example, the `(defaults) => string` form of `ui` only works on a single component), and no secrets. They can be overridden at runtime with `NUXT_PUBLIC_SHUO_UI_COMPONENTS_*` environment variables, as with any Nuxt runtimeConfig.

</warning>

## Size and UFormField

The size of every input component is decided in this order:

```text
size passed explicitly on the component
  >  size written on UFormField
  >  components.<component>.size
  >  formField theme default
  >  lg
```

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      Setup
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Result
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      Nothing set
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        lg
      </code>
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        <UFormField size="sm">
      </code>
      
       around <code>
        <ShuoInputText />
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        sm
      </code>
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        <UFormField size="sm">
      </code>
      
       around <code>
        <ShuoInputText size="xl" />
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        xl
      </code>
      
       (the component's own value wins)
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      Site-wide <code>
        inputText.size: 'md'
      </code>
      
      , no <code>
        size
      </code>
      
       on <code>
        UFormField
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        md
      </code>
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      Site-wide <code>
        inputText.size: 'md'
      </code>
      
      , <code>
        <UFormField size="sm">
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        sm
      </code>
      
       (a single field is closer than the site-wide setting)
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

"formField theme default" means `ui.formField.defaultVariants.size` in `app.config.ts` (`lg` in the built-in theme). It comes after the site-wide setting, so a `UFormField` without `size` does not override `components.<component>.size`; without a site-wide setting, the component uses it.

### Resizing every input component at once

This module has no cross-component `components.size`; `size` can only be set per component (`components.inputText.size`, `components.selectMenu.size` and so on). To resize every input component in your forms together, change the Nuxt UI `formField` theme default:

```ts [app.config.ts]
export default defineAppConfig({
  ui: {
    formField: { defaultVariants: { size: 'md' } }
  }
});
```

Every Shuo input component inside a `UFormField` becomes `md` when neither the component nor the `UFormField` sets `size` and there is no `components.<component>.size`. The `UFormField` label and description resize too. Limitations:

- Components outside a `UFormField` are not affected and stay at `components.<component>.size` or the built-in `lg`.
- Each component's `components.<component>.size` wins over this theme default. For example, with `components.selectMenu.size: 'lg'` also set, select menus stay `lg` and the other input components become `md`.
- A `size` written explicitly on the component or `UFormField` still wins.

## Query field columns

The built-in columns of `ShuoQueryCard` are `grid grid-cols-1 gap-x-5 gap-y-4 md:grid-cols-2 xl:grid-cols-4`. The site-wide `queryCard.ui.grid` is merged with them using tailwind-merge.

<warning>

tailwind-merge does not treat different breakpoints as conflicts: if you only write `md:grid-cols-3`, the built-in `xl:grid-cols-4` is kept and the layout goes back to 4 columns at xl width. So write out every breakpoint you use.

</warning>

```ts [nuxt.config.ts]
shuoUi: {
  components: {
    queryCard: {
      // 1 column on phones, 2 at sm, 3 at md and xl, 4 at 2xl
      ui: {
        grid: 'sm:grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-3 xl:grid-cols-3 2xl:grid-cols-4'
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Site-wide settings cannot contain functions, so you cannot fully replace the built-in columns there; when needed, pass `:ui="{ grid: () => '...' }"` on a single component.

**Tailwind scanning**: classes written in `nuxt.config.ts` must be inside Tailwind's scan range. Tailwind v4 scans the project root by default (excluding files in `.gitignore`), which usually includes `nuxt.config.ts`. If the classes do not apply, add an `@source` pointing at the config file in your project CSS:

```css [app/assets/css/main.css]
@import 'tailwindcss';
@import '@nuxt/ui';
@import '@shuo/ui/css';
@source '../../../nuxt.config.ts'; /* Path relative to this CSS file */
```

## Reading the effective value in a page

`resolveShuoDefault(component, prop)` returns the effective value, "site-wide setting ?? built-in default", for example so that the page size sent to the back end matches the list:

```ts
import type { PageRequest } from '#shuo-ui/types/pagination';

// The back end paginates by this value; if the page passes :page-size, use that value instead.
const pageSize = resolveShuoDefault('listCard', 'pageSize');
const request = reactive<PageRequest>({ PageNumber: 1, PageSize: pageSize });
```

`getShuoComponentDefaults()` returns your raw settings (without built-in defaults). See [Component defaults](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/utils/settings/component-defaults) under Utilities for the parameters of both functions.


# Locales and messages

> Component texts follow the Nuxt UI locale, and can be overridden per locale or extended with other locales.

Component texts (validation messages, accessible names, tooltips, date picker texts and so on) follow the Nuxt UI locale. Traditional Chinese (`zh-TW`) and English (`en`) are built in.

## Switching locales

Set the Nuxt UI locale on `UApp`; Nuxt UI and Shuo UI components switch together with no extra setup:

```vue [app.vue]
<template>
  <UApp :locale="locales[locale]">
    <NuxtPage />
  </UApp>
</template>

<script setup lang="ts">
import { en, zh_tw } from '@nuxt/ui/locale';

const locales = { 'zh-TW': zh_tw, en };
const locale = ref<keyof typeof locales>('zh-TW');
</script>
```

- Components pick texts by the `code` of the Nuxt UI locale (such as `zh-TW` or `en`), and components already on screen update immediately when it changes.
- With `@nuxtjs/i18n`, pass the Nuxt UI locale that matches the current locale to `UApp`; see Nuxt UI's [I18n](https://ui.nuxt.com/docs/getting-started/integrations/i18n/nuxt).
- Error messages of validation rules (`requiredText` and others) are produced at validation time, so validating again after switching gives the new locale.
- The month and weekday names of the date picker calendar follow the locale; the ROC or Gregorian year is still decided by `roc`.

### When no locale is set

When `UApp` has no `locale`, components use the module option `shuoUi.locale`, `zh-TW` by default. For an English-only project:

```ts [nuxt.config.ts]
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  shuoUi: { locale: 'en' }
});
```

### Locales that are not built in

When the Nuxt UI locale code is neither `zh-TW` nor `en`, components use, in order:

1. The texts set for this code in `shuoUi.locales` (see [Adding other locales](#adding-other-locales) below).
2. The built-in locale of the same language, for example English for `en-GB` and Traditional Chinese for `zh-CN`.
3. English.

## Overriding messages

`messages` overrides texts of the default locale (`shuoUi.locale`); only list what you want to change:

```ts [nuxt.config.ts]
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  shuoUi: {
    messages: {
      file: { placeholder: 'Choose an attachment' },
      listCard: { title: 'Results' }
    }
  }
});
```

Multilingual projects use `locales` to override texts per locale code; it takes precedence over `messages`:

```ts [nuxt.config.ts]
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  shuoUi: {
    locales: {
      // Traditional Chinese
      'zh-TW': { listCard: { title: '查詢清單' } },

      // English
      'en': {
        validation: { required: '{label} cannot be empty' },
        listCard: { title: 'Search results' }
      }
    }
  }
});
```

`{label}`, `{min}`, `{unit}`, `{total}`, `{start}`, `{end}`, `{year}` and `{month}` are placeholders that are replaced when used.

The `collapse` and `expand` texts of `queryCard` are put directly before the card title to form the aria-label of the collapse button, with no space added in between, so English texts end with a space (`'Collapse '` plus the title `Filters` gives `Collapse Filters`).

### Adding other locales

Add a locale code and its texts to `locales` to add a locale beyond the built-in ones. The code must match the `code` of the Nuxt UI locale. Untranslated items fall back to the built-in texts of the same language, or English:

```ts [nuxt.config.ts]
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  shuoUi: {
    locales: {
      ja: {
        queryCard: { title: '検索条件', submit: '検索' },
        listCard: { title: '検索結果' }
      }
    }
  }
});
```

<note>

An added locale does not change the language of the date picker calendar; month and weekday names use the built-in locale of the same language, or English.

</note>

    </td>

</tbody>
</table>

The built-in texts are in `node_modules/@shuo/ui/dist/runtime/locale/zh-tw.js` and `en.js`.

## Overriding a single component

A single component can also override texts with props, such as `<ShuoFile placeholder="..." />` or `<ShuoListCard title="..." empty="..." />`. These take precedence over the module settings and do not change with the locale.

<note>

`messages` and `locales` only hold texts. Put non-text site-wide settings, such as the select menu display format (`format`), sizes and page size, in [`components`](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/theme/component-defaults). Warnings shown in the console during development are always in Traditional Chinese.

</note>


# Module options

> Configure the component library with shuoUi in nuxt.config.ts.

## Usage

Configure it with `shuoUi` in `nuxt.config.ts`. These are the defaults:

```ts [nuxt.config.ts]
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['@nuxt/ui', '@shuo/ui'],
  shuoUi: {
    prefix: 'Shuo',
    theme: true,
    css: true,
    locale: 'zh-TW',
    messages: {},
    locales: {},
    components: {}
  }
});
```

## Options

<field-group>
<field default="Shuo" name="prefix" type="string">

Component name prefix. Change it to `My` to use `<MyInputText>`.

</field>

<field default="true" name="theme" type="boolean">

Whether to apply the built-in Nuxt UI theme; see [Theming](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/theme/theming#built-in-theme). `false` leaves it entirely to your project.

</field>

<field default="true" name="css" type="boolean">

Whether to load the default CSS variables (`--ui-form-*`); see [Form color tokens](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/theme/theming#form-color-tokens). `false` means your project defines them.

</field>

<field default="zh-TW" name="locale" type="string">

Default locale, used when the page sets no Nuxt UI locale (`<UApp :locale>`). `zh-TW` and `en` are built in; see [Locales and messages](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/theme/messages).

</field>

<field default="{}" name="messages" type="object">

Overrides texts of the default locale; only list what you want to change. See [Locales and messages](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/theme/messages#overriding-messages).

</field>

<field default="{}" name="locales" type="object">

Overrides texts per locale code, and can add locales beyond the built-in ones. See [Locales and messages](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/theme/messages#overriding-messages).

</field>

<field default="{}" name="components" type="object">

Global component defaults, grouped by component. See [Component defaults](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/theme/component-defaults).

</field>
</field-group>


# Theming

> Colors, form color tokens, the built-in theme, and how the per-component ui prop is merged.

## Colors come from your project

Components only use Nuxt UI semantic colors (`primary`, `neutral`, `error` and so on) and CSS variables, never hard-coded colors. Set your theme colors in your project's `app.config.ts`:

```ts [app.config.ts]
export default defineAppConfig({
  ui: { colors: { primary: 'blue', neutral: 'slate' } }
});
```

### Preview themes on the docs site

The palette button at the top right of the header switches the theme live. The whole site and every component example on the page follow it, just like the theme menu in the Nuxt UI docs:

- **Presets**: apply primary color, neutral color, font, icons and radius at once, then adjust each one. Items that differ from the preset are highlighted in the primary color.
- **Primary, Neutral, Font, Icons, Radius**: the same settings as Nuxt UI.
- **Component size, Date**: Shuo UI's global component defaults. They switch the `size` of every input component and the ROC / Gregorian year of the date picker at once. When you switch the icon set, the components' own icons (calendar, clear, download and so on) switch to the same set.
- **Component language**: the language of the component examples (Traditional Chinese or English). By default it follows the docs language; see [Locales and messages](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/theme/messages).
- **Color mode**: light, dark or system.
- **Export settings**: generates the `app.config.ts`, CSS and `nuxt.config.ts` for the current settings, listing only what differs from the defaults, ready to copy into your project.

Settings are stored only in your current browser and do not affect anyone else. Props passed explicitly in an example (such as a specific `calendar-icon` or `:roc="false"`) take precedence over these settings.

## Form color tokens

The colors of input borders and the disabled state come from the CSS variables below, with one set for light mode and one for dark mode. Disabled colors use the Nuxt UI neutral color, so their tone follows `ui.colors.neutral` in `app.config.ts`; borders use the primary color, with a lighter shade in dark mode:

```css
:root {
  --ui-form-border: var(--ui-color-primary-700); /* Input border */
  --ui-form-disabled-text: var(--ui-color-neutral-600); /* Disabled text */
  --ui-form-disabled-border: var(--ui-color-neutral-400); /* Disabled border */
  --ui-form-disabled-bg: var(--ui-color-neutral-100); /* Disabled background */
}

.dark {
  --ui-form-border: var(--ui-color-primary-400);
  --ui-form-disabled-text: var(--ui-color-neutral-400);
  --ui-form-disabled-border: var(--ui-color-neutral-600);
  --ui-form-disabled-bg: var(--ui-color-neutral-800);
}
```

To change them site-wide, redefine them in your project's CSS. The defaults loaded by the module have the lowest specificity, so no `!important` is needed. Writing only `:root` applies the same value in light and dark mode; to use different colors per mode, add `.dark` after `:root`:

```css [app/assets/css/main.css]
:root {
  --ui-form-disabled-bg: var(--ui-color-neutral-50);
}

.dark {
  --ui-form-disabled-bg: var(--ui-color-neutral-900);
}
```

## Built-in theme

With `theme: true`, the module adds the Nuxt UI theme below to `appConfig.ui` as **defaults** using `defu`; the `ui` settings in your project's `app.config.ts` take precedence.

To change one of them, override it in `app.config.ts`:

```ts [app.config.ts]
export default defineAppConfig({
  ui: {
    formField: {
      slots: { error: 'text-xs text-error' } // Use a regular error message style
    }
  }
});
```

<tip>

To skip the built-in theme entirely, set `shuoUi: { theme: false }` and configure `ui.input`, `ui.formField` and the rest yourself.

</tip>

## Per-component `ui` prop

A component's `ui` works like Nuxt UI's `ui` slots and only affects that component. To change every Nuxt UI component on the site, use `app.config.ts` as described in the previous section.

### Merge rules

- The component's built-in styles come first and the `ui` you pass comes after; they are merged with tailwind-merge, and your value wins when a slot conflicts. For example, `ShuoInputNumber` has a built-in `base: 'text-right'`; passing `{ base: 'text-center' }` centers the text while keeping the other built-in styles.
- When you pass a function `(defaults) => string`, `defaults` already contains the built-in styles and the return value is the final style, so you can replace them completely:

```vue
<ShuoInputNumber
  :ui="{
    base: (defaults) => defaults.replace('text-right', 'text-left')
  }"
/>
```

### Where `class` goes

The `class` you pass goes on the component's outer element, merged after `ui.root`, so it can override the built-in width (for example `class="w-14"`). The exceptions are:

      </code>
      
       goes on
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Use for the outer width
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

# v1.0.1

> Released on October 25, 2026

> `1.0.0` failed to build in projects without `@iconify-json/lucide` and has been withdrawn; use `1.0.1` instead. This release is the first stable version and includes the fix below.

The first stable release of Shuo UI: [Nuxt UI](https://ui.nuxt.com) components shaped around the way our projects write forms, shipped as a Nuxt module with 15 components. See the [docs site](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/) for full guides and live examples.

## ✨ Highlights

### 🧩 Built on Nuxt UI

The components wrap Nuxt UI. Nuxt UI props, slots and refs that are not redeclared can be used directly, with types inferred, so you can follow the Nuxt UI docs: [Built on Nuxt UI](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/overview/common#built-on-nuxt-ui)

```vue
<ShuoInputText v-model="keyword" variant="soft" icon="i-lucide-search" />
```

### 🇹🇼 Traditional Chinese and Taiwanese formats

Texts default to Traditional Chinese, with formats common in our projects built in: masked ID numbers, thousands separators, ROC-year dates, area codes and phone numbers, and year/month conversion. Bound values keep the raw data (Gregorian dates, plain numbers) and are only converted for display.

```vue
<ShuoInputText v-model="idNumber" :mask="4" />
<ShuoInputNumber v-model="amount" unit />
<!-- Shows 115/10/25; the bound value is 2026/10/25 -->
<ShuoDatepicker v-model="applyDate" />
```

### 📐 Consistent sizes and states

All form inputs share `size`, `disabled`, `loading`, `skeleton`, `id` and `name`. Components of the same size have the same height and follow the size, disabled and error states of `UFormField` and `UForm`: [Shared props](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/overview/common)

```vue
<UForm :schema="schema" :state="state" :disabled="saving">
  <UFormField label="Amount" name="amount" size="md">
    <ShuoInputNumber v-model="state.amount" :skeleton="loading" />
  </UFormField>
</UForm>
```

### ⚙️ Site-wide defaults and shared validation rules

Sizes, display formats, icons and more can be set once in `nuxt.config.ts`, while values passed on a component still win. Common Valibot rules are auto-imported, with consistent error messages across the site: [Component defaults](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/theme/component-defaults), [Validation](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/form/validation)

```ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['@nuxt/ui', '@shuo/ui'],
  shuoUi: {
    components: {
      selectMenu: { format: '{value}_{label}' },
      listCard: { pageSize: 20 }
    }
  }
});
```

```ts
const schema = v.object({
  name: requiredText('Name'),
  amount: requiredNumber('Amount')
});
```

### 🔎 Query page layout

`ShuoQueryCard` holds the query fields and `ShuoListCard` the results with server-side pagination, with loading skeletons, empty data and height transitions handled: [QueryCard](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/layout/query-card), [ListCard](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/layout/list-card)

## 🚀 New components

- **InputText:** Single-line text input that can mask all or the last characters ([docs](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/text/input-text))
- **InputNumber:** Number input with thousands separators after blur, configurable decimals and unit ([docs](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/text/input-number))
- **Textarea:** Multi-line text input that keeps line breaks and can resize automatically ([docs](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/text/textarea))
- **SelectMenu:** Select menu with search and multiple selection, showing the full text when truncated ([docs](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/choice/select-menu))
- **Datepicker:** Date picker with ROC years by default, five precisions and range selection ([docs](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/date/datepicker))
- **Checkbox:** Single checkbox with custom checked values and content next to the label ([docs](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/choice/checkbox))
- **RadioGroup:** Radio group that lays out by viewport width, with custom item fields and item content ([docs](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/choice/radio-group))
- **CheckboxGroup:** Checkbox group that lays out by viewport width, with custom item fields and item content ([docs](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/choice/checkbox-group))
- **File:** Single file selection and download of an existing attachment; selecting does not upload ([docs](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/phone-file/file))
- **Months:** Year and month input that can bind the total months, years and months at once ([docs](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/date/months))
- **Phone:** Landline number with separate inputs for the area code and number ([docs](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/phone-file/phone))
- **QueryCard:** Collapsible query card with a UForm inside and fields on a responsive grid ([docs](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/layout/query-card))
- **ListCard:** Results card with a title bar, table and server-side pagination ([docs](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/layout/list-card))
- **Table:** Plain table based on UTable, with skeletons, empty data and height transitions ([docs](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/layout/table))
- **InfoTooltip:** Info icon with a tooltip shown on hover or keyboard focus ([docs](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/helper/info-tooltip))

## 🐛 Bug Fixes

- **module:** Only icons from installed icon collections are added to the `@nuxt/icon` client bundle. `1.0.0` always added the built-in lucide icons, so `nuxt build` and `nuxt generate` failed to create the client bundle in projects without `@iconify-json/lucide`. Projects without it now build, and icons are loaded by `@nuxt/icon` at runtime. Installing `@iconify-json/lucide` is still recommended so icons are bundled into the site.

## ⚠️ Before you start

- Checkboxes and choice groups (`ShuoCheckbox`, `ShuoRadioGroup`, `ShuoCheckboxGroup`) match the height of inputs, so they do not support Nuxt UI descriptions (`description`, `descriptionKey`), `variant` (card, table), `indicator` or `highlight`. Passing them is a type error and they are not applied at runtime.
- `ShuoInputNumber` has no native `min`, `max` or `step`; use validation rules for ranges.
- Selecting a file does not upload it: `ShuoFile` only handles selection and download, and the page decides when to upload.

## 📦 Installation

```bash
pnpm add github:k90325248/shuo-ui#v1.0.1
pnpm add @iconify-json/lucide # recommended, icons are bundled
```

Enable the module in `nuxt.config.ts` and add `@import '@shuo/ui/css';` to your CSS; see [Installation](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/overview/installation) on the docs site.

  </tr>

    <td>
