# v1.1.0

> Released on October 26, 2026

Adds `ShuoTooltip`, so every tooltip can be shown with a long press on phones; component texts now follow the Nuxt UI locale, with Traditional Chinese and English built in. The docs site gains an English version and is reorganized into tabs and groups. Before upgrading, read "Upgrade notes" below: the auto-imported functions and the locale behavior of component texts have changed.

## ✨ Highlights

### 📱 Long press for tooltips on phones

Nuxt UI's `UTooltip` only opens on hover or keyboard focus, so tapping or holding on a phone shows nothing. The new `ShuoTooltip` keeps all `UTooltip` props and slots and adds long press on touch devices. `ShuoInfoTooltip` and the truncated-text tooltips of the select menu, datepicker, file, checkbox and choice groups all use it, so they also open with a long press on phones: [Tooltip](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/helper/tooltip)

```vue
<ShuoTooltip text="Save draft">
  <UButton label="Save" />
</ShuoTooltip>
```

A long press that shows a tooltip does not trigger the original click, check or menu. To keep Nuxt UI's original behavior, pass `:touch="false"` on a component or set `components.tooltip.touch: false` site-wide.

### 🌐 Component texts follow the Nuxt UI locale

Validation messages, accessible names, tooltips, and the months and weekdays of the datepicker follow `<UApp :locale>`, with Traditional Chinese and English built in; mounted components update immediately. Texts can be overridden per locale, and other locales can be added: [Locales and messages](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/theme/messages)

```ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  shuoUi: {
    locale: 'zh-TW', // used when the page does not set a UApp locale
    locales: {
      en: { listCard: { title: 'Search results' } }
    }
  }
});
```

### 🌙 Form color tokens for dark mode

Disabled inputs in dark mode now use a darker background and lighter text instead of the light mode colors, and input borders use a lighter primary color. The disabled color also changed from a fixed gray to Nuxt UI's neutral color, following `ui.colors.neutral` in your `app.config.ts`. The colors come from the `--ui-form-*` variables, which you can override in your CSS for `:root` and `.dark`: [Form color tokens](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/theme/theming#form-color-tokens)

## 🚀 New components

- **Tooltip:** Tooltip based on UTooltip that also opens with a long press on touch devices ([docs](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/helper/tooltip))

## 🐛 Bug Fixes

- **InputText:** Revealing masked text no longer briefly flashes the whole value.
- **Months:** The year and month units grow with their text, so the English `yr` and `mo` are no longer cut off.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

### Only public utility functions are auto-imported

The module used to auto-import every function under `runtime/utils` and `runtime/composables`, exposing internal helpers to projects. Now only the public functions below are auto-imported; see the new [Utilities](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/utils/form/validation) tab for parameters and examples:

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      Category
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Functions
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      Validation
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        requiredText
      </code>
      
      , <code>
        requiredNumber
      </code>
      
      , <code>
        requiredArray
      </code>
      
      , <code>
        optionalEmail
      </code>
      
      , <code>
        optionalNonNegativeNumber
      </code>
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      Formatting
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        formatDateDisplay
      </code>
      
      , <code>
        parseDateValue
      </code>
      
      , <code>
        formatNumberDisplay
      </code>
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      Field helpers
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        splitPhone
      </code>
      
      , <code>
        joinPhone
      </code>
      
      , <code>
        splitMonths
      </code>
      
      , <code>
        combineMonths
      </code>
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      Settings
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        resolveShuoDefault
      </code>
      
      , <code>
        getShuoComponentDefaults
      </code>
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

Internal functions such as `getShuoMessages`, `setShuoMessages`, `formatMessage`, `toNumberText`, `getDecimalPlaces`, `filterPhoneInput`, `getDateModelFormat`, `isValidDateSeparator`, `useChoiceGroup` and `useTruncatedText` are no longer auto-imported. If your project uses them, the build reports missing functions. They are not public API and may change, so use the public functions above or module options instead (for example, override texts with `shuoUi.messages` or `shuoUi.locales`).

### Component texts follow the UApp locale

Component texts used to be fixed to Traditional Chinese. Components now follow `<UApp :locale>`:

- Projects without a `UApp` `locale`, or with Traditional Chinese, look the same as before.
- Projects with another locale (for example English) will see component texts in that locale after upgrading. To adjust the wording, override it per locale with `shuoUi.locales`; see [Locales and messages](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/theme/messages#overriding-messages).

## 📖 Docs site

- **English version:** Switch between Traditional Chinese and English at the top right. URLs are now `/zh-tw/...` and `/en/...`, and the root URL redirects to the language you chose last. The 1.0.1 page URLs are no longer used; start again from the [home page](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/).
- **Tabs and groups:** Content is split into Getting started, Components and Utilities tabs, with the left menu grouped by purpose.
- **Theme menu:** The palette at the top right switches the primary color, font, radius, component size, ROC/Gregorian years and component locale on the fly, and exports the matching `app.config.ts`, CSS and `nuxt.config.ts`.

## 📦 Installation

```bash
pnpm add github:k90325248/shuo-ui#v1.1.0
pnpm add @iconify-json/lucide # recommended, icons are bundled
```

Enable the module in `nuxt.config.ts` and add `@import '@shuo/ui/css';` to your CSS; see [Installation](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/overview/installation) on the docs site.

# v1.2.0

> Released on October 27, 2026

Adds `ShuoSwitch`, which can call an API after toggling, updating only on success and reverting on failure; tables and list cards support row selection; checkboxes, choice groups and switches support descriptions. Component changelogs on the docs site now follow the docs language. Before upgrading, read "Upgrade notes" below: choice groups whose item data already has a `description` field will show it after upgrading.

## ✨ Highlights

### 🔀 A switch that confirms the change before updating

The new `ShuoSwitch` keeps the props of `USwitch` and adds `action`: after toggling, it shows the new value, loading and disabled. If the action returns `false` or throws, the switch reverts; any other result updates `v-model` and emits `change`. Use it for settings saved through an API as soon as they change: [Switch](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/choice/switch)

```vue
<ShuoSwitch v-model="enabled" label="Enable account" :action="(value) => api.setEnabled(value)" />
```

Its height matches inputs of the same size, and a long label is truncated with a tooltip showing the full text, the same as the checkbox. `size`, `color` and `loadingIcon` can be set site-wide with `components.switch`. Buttons need no wrapper: `loading-auto` on `UButton` already provides the same loading state.

### ☑️ Row selection in tables and list cards

With `selectable`, `ShuoTable` and `ShuoListCard` add a selection column at the front, and the selection is bound to an array of keys with `v-model:selected`: [Selection in Table](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/layout/table#selection)

```vue
<ShuoListCard
  v-model:selected="selected"
  :data="rows"
  :columns="columns"
  selectable
  row-key="ID"
  :row-selectable="(row) => row.status !== 'Closed'"
  @page-change="search"
/>
```

- `row-key` is a field name or a function. With server-side pagination, selections on other pages are kept when changing pages, so rows selected across pages can be handled together.
- Select all in the header only selects the selectable rows on the current page and shows an indeterminate state when only some are selected; with `select-all` set to `false`, the header shows the `selection-header` text instead.
- Rows for which `row-selectable` returns `false` cannot be selected; all checkboxes are disabled while loading.
- `checkbox-props` sets the `class`, `ui`, `color`, `size` and icons of the checkboxes. Put `{ id: 'select' }` in `columns` to place the selection column, or replace it entirely with the `#select-header` and `#select-cell` slots.
- `selectAll` and `checkboxProps` can be set site-wide with `components.table`.

Without `selectable` nothing changes, and controlling selection yourself through `tableProps` still works.

### 📝 Descriptions on checkboxes, choice groups and switches

`ShuoCheckbox`, `ShuoRadioGroup`, `ShuoCheckboxGroup` and `ShuoSwitch` support descriptions (for groups, the item's `description` field or the field set by `description-key`). Without a description the height still matches inputs; with one the control grows and the description wraps, while the first line stays aligned with the fields next to it. In horizontal groups the whole row grows, and the description does not squeeze the labels of other items: [Checkbox description](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/choice/checkbox#description)

```vue
<ShuoCheckbox
  v-model="subscribe"
  label="Subscribe to the newsletter"
  description="A weekly email; unsubscribe at any time"
/>
```

## 🚀 New components

- **Switch:** Switch that can run an action after toggling, updating the bound value only on success and reverting on failure or errors ([docs](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/choice/switch))

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

### The description field of items is shown

Radio and checkbox groups used to hide item descriptions, ignoring any `description` field in the item data. It is now shown below the item label and makes the item taller.

If your items come straight from back-end data that happens to have a `description` field (for example remarks in a code table), the page will show it after upgrading. To hide it, remove the field before passing the items:

```ts
const options = computed(() => codes.value.map(({ description: _description, ...item }) => item));
```

## 📖 Docs site

- **Releases:** A new Releases tab in the header shows the release notes of every version, the same as the GitHub Releases, in English on the English site.
- **Localized changelogs:** The changelog at the end of each component page now shows English or Chinese text by docs language, without `feat:` or `fix:` prefixes.
- **New pages:** A new [Switch](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/choice/switch) page; the Table, ListCard, Checkbox, RadioGroup and CheckboxGroup pages add usage and examples for selection and descriptions; the examples on the shared props page include the switch.

## 📦 Installation

```bash
pnpm add github:k90325248/shuo-ui#v1.2.0
pnpm add @iconify-json/lucide # recommended, icons are bundled
```

Enable the module in `nuxt.config.ts` and add `@import '@shuo/ui/css';` to your CSS; see [Installation](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/overview/installation) on the docs site.

# Months

> Splitting total months into years and months, and combining them back.

## Usage

[Months](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/date/months) binds the total months, and can also bind `year` and `month`. For list display, or when the back end stores years and months separately, convert with these two functions:

```vue
<template>
  <ShuoListCard :data="rows" :columns="columns">
    <!-- Loan term -->
    <template #terms-cell="{ row }">
      {{ toYearMonth(row.original.terms) }}
    </template>
  </ShuoListCard>
</template>

<script setup lang="ts">
// Total months as "2 yr 6 mo"; empty values show an empty string.
const toYearMonth = (terms: number | null) => {
  const months = splitMonths(terms);
  return months ? `${months.year} yr ${months.month} mo` : '';
};
</script>
```

The functions are auto-imported by the module. Both return the same result type:

```ts
interface MonthsValue {
  total: number; // Total months
  year: number; // Full years
  month: number; // Remaining months, 0 to 11
}
```

## API

### splitMonths

```ts
splitMonths(value: unknown): MonthsValue | null
```

Splits total months into years and months. Only non-negative safe integers are accepted; empty values, negative numbers, decimals and non-numbers return `null`.

<field-group>
<field :required="true" name="value" type="unknown">

Total months.

</field>
</field-group>

### combineMonths

```ts
combineMonths(
  year: number | null | undefined,
  month: number | null | undefined
): MonthsValue | null
```

Combines years and months and carries over, for example 1 year 14 months becomes 2 years 2 months. An empty side counts as `0`, and when both are empty it returns `null`; negative numbers or non-integers return `null`.

<field-group>
<field :required="true" name="year" type="number | null | undefined">

Years.

</field>

<field :required="true" name="month" type="number | null | undefined">

Months; can be more than 11.

</field>
</field-group>

## Examples

```ts
splitMonths(30); // { total: 30, year: 2, month: 6 }
splitMonths(null); // null
splitMonths(1.5); // null

combineMonths(2, 6); // { total: 30, year: 2, month: 6 }
combineMonths(1, 14); // { total: 26, year: 2, month: 2 }
combineMonths(null, 8); // { total: 8, year: 0, month: 8 }
combineMonths(null, null); // null
```


# Phone

> Splitting and joining the area code of landline numbers.

## Usage

[Phone](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/phone-file/phone) binds the full number with `v-model`, and can also bind `area-code` and `number`. When the back end stores the area code and number separately, or the screen shows them separately, convert with these two functions:

```ts
// The back end returns the full number and area code; split them into two fields
const { areaCode, number } = splitPhone(data.phone, data.areaCode);

// Join them before submitting
const phone = joinPhone(state.areaCode, state.number);
```

The functions are auto-imported by the module. Numbers contain only digits, with no separators such as `-` or parentheses.

## API

### splitPhone

```ts
splitPhone(
  value: string | undefined,
  areaCode: string | undefined
): { areaCode: string | undefined; number: string | undefined }
```

Splits the full number by a known area code. Taiwanese area codes vary in length, so it never guesses the length when the area code is unknown: when the area code is empty or the number does not start with it, the area code is returned as an empty string and the full number goes in `number`.

<field-group>
<field :required="true" name="value" type="string | undefined">

The full number. When `undefined` or an empty string, both the area code and the number return the same value.

</field>

<field :required="true" name="areaCode" type="string | undefined">

The known area code, such as `02`.

</field>
</field-group>

### joinPhone

```ts
joinPhone(
  areaCode: string | undefined,
  number: string | undefined
): string | undefined
```

Joins the area code and number with no separator. When both are `undefined`, it returns `undefined` (meaning not initialized yet); when only one is `undefined`, it counts as an empty string.

<field-group>
<field :required="true" name="areaCode" type="string | undefined">

The area code.

</field>

<field :required="true" name="number" type="string | undefined">

The phone number.

</field>
</field-group>

## Examples

```ts
splitPhone('0223456789', '02'); // { areaCode: '02', number: '23456789' }
splitPhone('0223456789', '03'); // { areaCode: '', number: '0223456789' }
splitPhone('0223456789', undefined); // { areaCode: '', number: '0223456789' }

joinPhone('02', '23456789'); // '0223456789'
joinPhone(undefined, undefined); // undefined
```


# Validation

> Shared validation rules for Valibot, with consistent error messages across the site.

## Usage

The rules are auto-imported by the module and return Valibot schemas, so put them straight into `v.object` to build a form schema:

```ts
import * as v from 'valibot';

const schema = v.object({
  name: requiredText('Name'),
  amount: requiredNumber('Amount'),
  types: requiredArray('Types', v.string())
});
```

- The `label` parameter is the field name on screen; the default error message is "field name + description", for example "Name is required". Messages follow the Nuxt UI locale and are produced at validation time, so validating again after switching gives the new locale. Override them with the module option `shuoUi.messages.validation` or `shuoUi.locales`; see [Locales and messages](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/theme/messages).
- The input types accept `null` and `undefined` while editing, and the output after validation narrows to `string`, `number` or an array, so you do not need to change the components' empty-value contract.
- See [Validation](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/form/validation) for forms, empty values and error display as a whole.

<note>

If your project uses `import * as v from 'valibot'`, install `valibot` as well (`pnpm add valibot`); pnpm does not let a project import a package's dependencies directly.

</note>

## API

### requiredText

```ts
requiredText(label: string)
```

Required text. Rejects `null`, `undefined`, empty strings, whitespace only and non-string values, and keeps the original text (no trimming). For text inputs, multi-line text, string values of select menus and radio groups, and date strings.

<field-group>
<field :required="true" name="label" type="string">

Field name, used in the error message.

</field>
</field-group>

### requiredNumber

```ts
requiredNumber(label: string)
```

Required number. Accepts `0`, negative numbers and decimals; empty values and strings show "is required", and `NaN` and infinity show "must be a valid number".

<field-group>
<field :required="true" name="label" type="string">

Field name, used in the error message.

</field>
</field-group>

### requiredArray

```ts
requiredArray(label: string, itemSchema: GenericSchema)
```

Required array with at least one item. Empty arrays, `null` and `undefined` fail. For checkbox groups and multiple select menus.

<field-group>
<field :required="true" name="label" type="string">

Field name, used in the error message.

</field>

<field :required="true" name="itemSchema" type="GenericSchema">

The schema of each item, such as `v.string()`; the valid option values are composed by each page rather than fixed in the shared rule.

</field>
</field-group>

### optionalEmail

```ts
optionalEmail(label: string)
```

Optional email. Empty strings pass; a value must be a valid email, otherwise "has an invalid format" is shown. For a required email, chain `v.email` after `requiredText` instead.

<field-group>
<field :required="true" name="label" type="string">

Field name, used in the error message.

</field>
</field-group>

### optionalNonNegativeNumber

```ts
optionalNonNegativeNumber(label: string)
```

Optional non-negative number. `null` passes; `0` and decimals are accepted; negative numbers show "must be at least 0", and `NaN`, infinity and non-numbers show "must be a valid number". For optional fields such as amounts, terms, scores and rates.

<field-group>
<field :required="true" name="label" type="string">

Field name, used in the error message.

</field>
</field-group>

## Examples

### Combining with other Valibot rules

The shared rules are ordinary Valibot schemas, so you can add conditions with `v.pipe`:

```ts
import * as v from 'valibot';

const schema = v.object({
  // Required email: the required rule followed by a format check
  email: v.pipe(requiredText('Email'), v.email('Email is invalid')),

  // Optional whole number of terms
  terms: v.pipe(
    optionalNonNegativeNumber('Terms'),
    v.check(
      (value) => value === null || Number.isInteger(value),
      'Terms must be a whole number'
    )
  ),

  // The backup email can be left empty
  backupEmail: optionalEmail('Backup email')
});
```

### In a form

See "With form validation" on each component page for complete forms with live examples, such as [InputText](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/text/input-text) and [SelectMenu](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/choice/select-menu).

---

- [Valibot](https://valibot.dev/guides/introduction/)


# Date

> ROC year display and strict parsing of Gregorian date strings.

## Usage

Bound values and API data always stay Gregorian, and are converted to ROC years only for display. Call it directly in the template for lists, detail views and so on:

```vue
<template>
  <ShuoListCard :data="rows" :columns="columns">
    <!-- Application date -->
    <template #applyDate-cell="{ row }">
      {{ formatDateDisplay(row.original.applyDate) }}
    </template>
  </ShuoListCard>
</template>
```

- The functions are auto-imported by the module, with no import needed.
- Date strings can use `/` or `-` as the separator, with the time after a space; months, days, hours, minutes and seconds must have two digits. ISO strings with `T`, `Z` or a time zone are not accepted, and there is no time zone conversion.
- See [Datepicker](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/date/datepicker) for the date picker's bound format and `mode`.

## API

### formatDateDisplay

```ts
formatDateDisplay(
  value: string | Date | null | undefined,
  options?: DateDisplayOptions
): string
```

Converts a Gregorian date to display text, ROC year-month-day by default. Empty values, invalid dates and strings that do not match the precision return an empty string; in ROC mode, dates before 1911 also return an empty string.

<field-group>
<field name="value" type="string | Date | null | undefined" :required="true">

A Gregorian date string or `Date`. A string must match the `mode` precision, for example `2026/10` for `mode: 'month'`.

</field>

<field name="options.mode" type="'year' | 'month' | 'date' | 'datetime' | 'datetime-second'">

Date precision, `date` by default.

</field>

<field name="options.roc" type="boolean">

Whether to show ROC years, `true` by default; `false` shows Gregorian years.

</field>

<field name="options.yearMonthLabels" type="boolean | { year: string; month: string }">

Adds units to years and year-months, `false` by default. `true` uses the current locale's format ("10/115" in English, "115 年 10 月" in Traditional Chinese); you can also pass formats, where `{year}` and `{month}` are the year and the two-digit month, for example `{ year: 'Year {year}', month: '{month}/{year}' }`.

</field>
</field-group>

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      mode
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Gregorian string
    </th>
    
    <th>
      ROC display
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        year
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        2026
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        115
      </code>
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        month
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        2026/10
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        115/10
      </code>
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        date
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        2026/10/15
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        115/10/15
      </code>
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        datetime
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        2026/10/15 09:08
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        115/10/15 09:08
      </code>
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        datetime-second
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        2026/10/15 09:08:07
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        115/10/15 09:08:07
      </code>
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### parseDateValue

```ts
parseDateValue(
  value: string | null | undefined,
  mode: DateMode,
  separator?: string
): Date | null
```

Strictly parses a Gregorian date string. The format must exactly match the given precision and separator (two digits, a date that exists), otherwise it returns `null`. Useful for checking a date string before submitting.

<field-group>
<field name="value" type="string | null | undefined" :required="true">

A Gregorian date string.

</field>

<field name="mode" type="'year' | 'month' | 'date' | 'datetime' | 'datetime-second'" :required="true">

Date precision.

</field>

<field name="separator" type="string">

Date separator, `/` by default; pass the same value when the date picker sets `separator`.

</field>
</field-group>

## Examples

### Display format

```ts
formatDateDisplay('2026/10/15'); // 115/10/15
formatDateDisplay('2026-10-15'); // 115/10/15
formatDateDisplay('2026/10/15', { roc: false }); // 2026/10/15
formatDateDisplay('2026', { mode: 'year' }); // 115
formatDateDisplay('2026/10', {
  mode: 'month',
  yearMonthLabels: true
}); // 10/115 in English (115 年 10 月 in Traditional Chinese)
formatDateDisplay('2026/10/15 09:08', { mode: 'datetime' }); // 115/10/15 09:08
formatDateDisplay('2026/02/30'); // '' (the date does not exist)
formatDateDisplay(null); // ''
```

### Strict parsing

```ts
parseDateValue('2026/10/15', 'date'); // Date
parseDateValue('2026/1/5', 'date'); // null (month and day not two digits)
parseDateValue('2026/02/30', 'date'); // null (the date does not exist)
parseDateValue('2026-10-15', 'date', '-'); // Date
```


# Number

> Number display with thousands separators and fixed decimal places.

## Usage

API data and bound values stay numbers and are formatted only for display. Call it directly in the template for list columns, without creating a separate formatter:

```vue
<template>
  <ShuoListCard :data="rows" :columns="columns">
    <!-- Amount -->
    <template #amount-cell="{ row }">
      {{ formatNumberDisplay(row.original.amount) }}
    </template>
  </ShuoListCard>
</template>
```

The function is auto-imported by the module and uses the same rules as [InputNumber](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/components/text/input-number) shows after blur. Do not write strings with commas or padded zeros back into the data.

## API

### formatNumberDisplay

```ts
formatNumberDisplay(
  value: number | null | undefined,
  decimal?: boolean | number,
  thousandSeparator?: boolean
): string
```

Converts a number to display text. `null`, `undefined`, `NaN` and infinity return an empty string, and `0` shows normally; very large or very small numbers are written out in full, never in scientific notation.

<field-group>
<field name="value" type="number | null | undefined" :required="true">

The number to display.

</field>

<field name="decimal" type="boolean | number">

Decimal places, `true` by default. `true` keeps the original decimals without padding; `false` or `0` rounds to an integer; a positive integer fixes the number of places, padding with zeros or rounding as needed, up to 100 places.

</field>

<field name="thousandSeparator" type="boolean">

Whether to add thousands separators, `true` by default.

</field>
</field-group>

<note>

The `decimal` of `ShuoInputNumber` defaults to `false` (integers only), unlike the default here, which keeps decimals.

</note>

## Examples

```ts
formatNumberDisplay(1234567); // 1,234,567
formatNumberDisplay(-1234.5); // -1,234.5
formatNumberDisplay(1234.5, 3); // 1,234.500
formatNumberDisplay(1234.5, 3, false); // 1234.500
formatNumberDisplay(1234.5, false); // 1,235
formatNumberDisplay(0.1 + 0.2, 2); // 0.30
formatNumberDisplay(0); // 0
formatNumberDisplay(null); // ''
```


# ComponentDefaults

> Read the effective values and raw settings of the component defaults in a page.

## Usage

Site-wide component defaults are set in `shuoUi.components` in `nuxt.config.ts`; see [Component defaults](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/theme/component-defaults). When a page needs the same value the component uses (for example, the page size sent to the back end must match the list), get it with `resolveShuoDefault`:

```ts
import type { PageRequest } from '#shuo-ui/types/pagination';

// The back end paginates by this value; if the page passes :page-size, use that value instead.
const pageSize = resolveShuoDefault('listCard', 'pageSize');
const request = reactive<PageRequest>({ PageNumber: 1, PageSize: pageSize });
```

The functions are auto-imported by the module.

## API

### resolveShuoDefault

```ts
resolveShuoDefault(name: ShuoComponentName, key: string)
```

Returns the effective default of a component prop: the setting when there is a site-wide one, otherwise the component's built-in default. Items whose built-in default is `undefined` (such as `textarea.rows`) return `undefined` when not set. The return type is inferred from the component and prop.

<field-group>
<field :required="true" name="name" type="ShuoComponentName">

Component key, the same as the keys of `shuoUi.components`, such as `listCard` or `selectMenu`.

</field>

<field :required="true" name="key" type="string">

The name of a prop that can be set site-wide, such as `pageSize`; only items in that component's list are accepted. See [Configurable props](https://k90325248.github.io/shuo-ui/getting-started/theme/component-defaults#configurable-props).

</field>
</field-group>

### getShuoComponentDefaults

```ts
getShuoComponentDefaults(): ShuoComponentDefaults
```

Returns your raw settings in `shuoUi.components`, with only the items you set and none of the components' built-in defaults; use `resolveShuoDefault` for effective values.

## Examples

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts sets listCard.pageSize: 20 and no selectMenu.format
resolveShuoDefault('listCard', 'pageSize'); // 20
resolveShuoDefault('selectMenu', 'format'); // '{label}' (built-in default)

getShuoComponentDefaults(); // { listCard: { pageSize: 20 } }
```
